# Submission and runtime boundaries

Submit a regular directory `submission/` with a regular UTF-8 `main.py`. Supporting modules, data and subdirectories are allowed: at most8MiB total regular-file bytes and256 entries including directories. Symlinks, multiply-linked files and special files are rejected for collection safety. NumPy1.26.4, ONNX Runtime1.16.3 and their pinned dependencies are bundled under /workspace/vendor; native runtime libraries are under /workspace/native. No download, training or native compilation is needed. Standard-library, bundled-package and submitted-module imports are allowed. Only frozen submission bytes are executed; editing public runner/checker/protocol files does not affect verification. The task provides CPython 3.11.14 on Linux x86-64, CPU only.

Each invocation handles the **whole** batch within 150 seconds wall time. Local worker limits are 180 CPU seconds soft /181 hard per process, 2 GiB address space per process, 64 processes/threads per reserved UID for the outer generic worker; the candidate child itself is restricted to one process/one thread by the public runner, 256 open descriptors per process, 64 MiB per regular file, zero core dumps. The inherited generic worker uses at most its first two available CPUs (no exclusive cores). Input ≤16 MiB, stdout ≤32 MiB, stderr ≤1 MiB. Limits apply to errors too; output overflow, empty/non-JSON/wrong output, nonzero exit, or timeout fails the invocation. A normal zero exit, including `os._exit(0)`, is accepted only if complete correct JSON actually reaches the stdout pipe. Text stdin/stdout, .buffer, raw descriptors 0/1, fileno(), and fdopen() all work. The public checker executes a separate bounded child and checks its actual bytes and exit status.

The local trial runs as a nonprivileged reserved UID in an allowlisted chroot with immutable runtime/source and clean environment. Only `/workspace/tmp` is writable and is cleared between invocations; it need not be used. Runtime files and standard `/dev/null`, `/dev/zero`, `/dev/random`, `/dev/urandom` are available; only a read-only /proc/cpuinfo CPU-descriptor snapshot is exposed (needed by the bundled inference runtime); no process /proc entries, /sys, credentials, private verifier, or solution is mounted. Networking (including loopback) is disabled. Socket/socketpair/connect; System V shared memory/semaphore/message queues; kill/tkill/tgkill; ptrace/process_vm_readv/process_vm_writev; unshare/setns; mount/umount2/pivot_root/chroot; setsid/setpgid; identity/group changes; open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at; bpf; keyctl/add_key/request_key; perf_event_open; userfaultfd; io_uring operations; and pidfd_getfd are denied with EPERM. The outer generic filter marks clone3 unavailable; the candidate runner returns EPERM for clone3, as observed in the actual child profile. Namespace-creating clone flags are denied. The candidate runner additionally denies fork, vfork, clone and clone3, so a candidate cannot create subprocesses/threads. Its parent can still launch the candidate and cleanly reap it. The runner also independently denies socket/socketpair/connect, kill/tkill/tgkill, ptrace, process_vm_readv/process_vm_writev, pidfd_open and pidfd_send_signal in the candidate child; its parent retains pidfd-based cleanup. The outer profile supplies the remaining listed restrictions. Non-x86-64 and x32 syscall ABIs are terminated. No resources outside this contract are necessary.

The worker sets PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, HOME=/workspace, LANG=LC_ALL=C, TMPDIR=/workspace/tmp, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/workspace/native, and OpenBLAS/OMP/MKL thread counts to 1. Source is run with -B; no site customization is submitted. Scratch is monitored approximately every 0.25 seconds: >1 GiB max(logical,allocated) file bytes or >50000 path entries triggers an **infrastructure error with no score**, not a precise quota. This local profile has no hard aggregate cgroup CPU/memory/storage guarantee and shares the host kernel. It is a local development/trial profile, not proof of hostile-kernel isolation. Formal container/transport validation remains pending separately.

`python3 public_check.py [--candidate PATH]` uses only this public workspace. Run it inside the supplied container or equivalent unprivileged development environment. It is a sanity checker and does not establish isolation by itself. It sets the same child resource limits, wall/output bounds and no-fork/no-socket filter without root; an outer container or worker supplies filesystem/UID and the remaining syscall restrictions. `python3 public_exec.py PATH` uses the same bounded child and relays its actual output/exit for local grading. Descendant creation is prevented, not left to an unbounded process-tree scan. It returns nonzero for candidate failure and never writes a reward. The private formal verifier is a separate image and remains fail-closed pending infrastructure validation. Runtime is a feasibility budget, not an optimization score or hardware-performance metric.

Bundled dependency versions: tqdm4.67.1, coloredlogs15.0.1, humanfriendly10.0, flatbuffers24.3.25, packaging24.2, protobuf4.25.3, sympy1.13.3, mpmath1.3.0. Models and dependency files are public and outside the submission collection budget. The public entry adds /workspace/vendor to sys.path. Native libraries use the bundled Ubuntu20.04 x86-64 libstdc++/libgcc10.5.0 and zlib1.2.11 copies; no native library path outside the public runtime is required.

The public runner observes SIGTERM/SIGINT during both pipe transfer and the final process-exit wait, including when the child has closed all pipes but stays alive. Repeated signals only mark cancellation while cleanup finishes. The child is killed and reaped before run returns or raises; the public checker stops starting fixtures after cancellation. Closing pipes is not process completion, a successful result or an escape from the same whole-batch deadline.
=== README
FENIX CPU controller workspace

Implement submission/controller.py and any supporting modules. The project
includes fixed model assets, CPU inference, probability compilation, sequence
loading and classification metrics. The planner is unfinished.

Read PROTOCOL.md and LIMITS.md. Run `python3 public_check.py` from /workspace.
The check executes the submitted main.py as a separate bounded process.
All dependencies are bundled for offline use; no training or accelerator is required.
=== instruction
Extend the FENIX CPU controller to plan certified feature-window exports.
Work in `/workspace/submission`; the model evaluators, probability compiler and metric code are supplied.
Read `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md` for the complete version3 schema, mathematical objective and certificate coordinates.
Read `/workspace/LIMITS.md` for submission, whole-batch and process restrictions.
Your entry is `python3 -B /workspace/submission/main.py`, with one JSON request on stdin and one JSON response on stdout.
Validate the entire request before returning results; invalid input must return `{"error":"invalid"}` and exit0.
For each epoch classify every nine-packet window using its selected bundled CPU model.
Compile the probability table and use its sampled range thresholds to determine eligibility.
Plan exports jointly across reserved service slots and finite token inventory with refill saturation.
Respect window readiness/expiry, per-flow ceilings and all ancestor-group ceilings.
Maximize minimum normalized flow coverage, then predicted-class utility, then minimize waiting age.
Return a schedule, exact objective values, a feasible circulation and residual potentials.
Also prove maximal coverage with the specified next-ratio infeasibility cut when coverage is below1.
Any schedule or certificate satisfying the stated requirements is accepted; no extra tie-break applies.
Report selected-window and flow-vote classification metrics, including empty selections.
The controller planner is unfinished; supplied CPU inference and table primitives need no training or hardware.
Supporting modules and data are allowed within the published submission budget.
Run `python3 public_check.py` from `/workspace` for a small sanity check.
The check launches your actual program through bounded stdin/stdout pipes.
It covers only a small example and wire behavior; implement the full published domain.
